title: The methodology's front-matter container
description: A backbone file schema (ADR-056): the one key the methodology owns inside an artefact's front matter or a collection entry (COR-053 point 10) — `pkit` in this distribution. Everything under it is the methodology's; everything outside it is the artefact's own and is not constrained here. Inside the container a functionality block is named for its functionality (`friction`, COR-050) and carries no version; any other key is a role block whose every child is a point block carrying the integer `schema_version` of the point it targets. The discrimination between a misspelt key and a role block, the nearest-known-key suggestion and orphan reporting are applied by `project_kit.backbone_schemas` on top of this shape. Bound by location — the front matter of a document, or a collection entry, in a declared place — never by a field. Backbone-owned; carries no version of its own and is migrated when it changes (COR-010).

carrier.title: A document's front matter, or a collection entry
carrier.description: The object that carries the container. Both forms are the same shape today: an object with the artefact's own keys and, optionally, the methodology's `pkit` key. They are named separately below so a later divergence lands in one place.

document-front-matter.title: Document form
document-front-matter.description: The front matter of a Markdown document in a declared place (COR-050 point 1).

collection-entry.title: Collection-entry form
collection-entry.description: One keyed entry of a collection file whose front matter maps entries by id (COR-050 point 1). The entry's id is the key it sits under, outside this object; the entry object carries the same container as a document's front matter.

container.title: The container (the value under `pkit`)
container.description: Functionality blocks by name; every other key is a role block. See the module for how validation reads it.

friction.title: The `friction` functionality block (COR-050)
friction.description: Anchors — or, for an artefact with nothing to anchor to, the reason a person accepted it with none — the last revalidation on a person's decision, and a tool-written `last-check` status. Backbone-owned: no version; unknown keys refused (COR-050 point 2).

unanchored-because.description: Why the artefact has no anchors: the reason a person accepted it unanchored, such as a role no code embodies (COR-050 point 1). The unanchored measure lists such an artefact apart, with this reason, and counts only those without one (point 8). It stands instead of anchors, never beside them: validation refuses the pair (point 12), with its own finding rather than a shape error here.

anchors.title: Anchors, grouped by kind (COR-050 point 2)
anchors.description: The three kinds the backbone resolves. A kind a capability registers is not admitted here until the kind registry exists; validation then reads registered kinds the way the container reads role blocks.

path.description: Files or globs relative to the repository root; `**` matches across folders.

revalidated.title: The last revalidation (COR-050 points 3 and 4)
revalidated.description: Written on a person's decision. `at` is the marker of a revalidation and comes with its `outcome`; `unchanged` requires `unchanged-because`. An artefact never yet revalidated may carry `deferred` alone; an empty block is refused.

at.description: UTC timestamp of the revalidation; changes on every revalidation.

unchanged-because.description: Why the content still holds against this change; required with `outcome: unchanged`.

deferred.description: One entry per anchor whose friction is deliberately postponed, kept sorted by anchor.

anchor-reference.title: An anchor written as its kind and value

last-check.title: The tool-written status (COR-050 point 10)
last-check.description: Written only by the after-merge job, never read for friction. `state` is what the check found, `as-of` the commit it was checked against, `since` where any staleness came from.

as-of.description: The commit the check ran against.

since.description: Where the staleness came from: the commit at which the first changed anchor moved past the revalidation point.

role-block.title: A role block (COR-053 point 10)
role-block.description: Named for a role — the role word alone, or its qualified form `<publisher>::<role>` when two active roles share a word or the word equals a functionality block's name. Keyed by point; every point block carries the point's `schema_version`. The point's own schema, shipped by the role's provider, validates the rest of the block.

point-block.title: A point block
point-block.description: The data a role's provider keeps about the artefact for one point. Only `schema_version` is fixed here; the body is validated by the provider's point schema at a compatible version, and left alone otherwise (inert, COR-052 point 5).
